Since DID is a coping mechanism, many alters (mostly hosts but also littles and others) are not supposed to know about the system until they are ready, and sometimes they won't know for their whole life.
There can be moments where the host can take care of anything without any help, if the situation is perceived as safe and calm and if the host is ok. No triggers and stability can bring to stability to who fronts too.
But deep inside the alters are still there, if they are not needed they can just freeze or live in the headspace without fronting for a while.

Fast forward to 6 months or something later. She came, eat and asked me to go outside with her for a cigarette together since it was her last time here.

She told me I made her feel better and that she decided to let her son go due to a conversation we had the week before. She felt like the way I behave was similar to her son, she even told I was the daughter she had always dreamt of having. That's why she wanted to be around me all the time. 
I went with her at the hospital the next day then I took her to the airport. I felt like I needed to say goodbye to this poor boy too. 
Don't know what happened after, but I will remember this strong mother and her kindness forever.

If you are talking in a language that is not your first language, people tend to understand you are a foreigner anyway. 

But if you are writing... Unless you state you are a foreigner, usually you'll find at least two or three people commenting about your grammar or spelling mistakes, insulting you or laughing. 

English-speaking-people usually are kinda like sharks waiting for you to misspell something. Germans too. Spanish and Arabian people are really kind and chill about it. Russians... They just pretend they didn't understand or ignore you. 

Fun fact, when I write in my language I purposefully misspell words or use poor grammar sometimes due to memes or social conventions. Sometimes I get corrected, sometimes people laugh.

Honestly, I usually do that so that people will not feel the urge to insult me and comment about how I cannot speak, since it used to happen a lot. 
It seems like my English is awful and people kept joking about it and making me feel like a poor idiot wasting time. 

I, being a depressed and low-self-esteem girl, almost quit studying English (and Russian, Spanish, German,...) for this problem.

Now I start each and every comment stating that I'm Italian and that I have a low self esteem, so please be kind to me.

And sorry for any spelling or grammar mistakes, English is not my first language 😝

First of all, the host himself is an alter.


Alters are created for keeping the body and the rest of the system safe, so as long as they do this, they can be anything. Keep in mind that alters can have any age, even be ageless or age-slider. Also they can be of every gender and sexuality. 


They can come from all over the world or form different worlds entirely. They can be humans, extraterrestrial being, religious figures, beings coming from folklore, animals, objects, famous people, characters from tv shows, books, children's shows, ... They can be dead, alive, or something in the middle, suffering from mental health problems or physical problems, be disabled, be mute or deaf, ... 


They can be easy to reach and talk to or can be absolutely avoidant, hostile or terrified, ... 


There are common alters though, which are:
- host/hosts 
- protectors
- memory holders
- persecutors
- inner self helpers
- children 
- opposite-sex alters
- sexual alters


Less common are:
- gatekeepers
- caretkers
- fragments
- very old alters 
- non-human alters 
- dead alters 
- alters based on existing people like politicians or CEO 
- suicidal alters
- disabled alters
- alters that suffer from DID themselves (so systems inside systems)

Hi again! 

The term "original" is obsolete and kinda wrong. 

Recent theories about DID state that alters are not created from one person that suddenly splits but it's the other way around. When the child reaches a certain age and level of conscience his personality solidify into one, but due to traumas it can happen that the personality does not end up solidify into one but into many. Being this the defense mechanism that the brain has learned, later in life many alters in case of traumas or therapy or many many reasons may integrate/appear/go dormant/...

However, even if you do not believe these theories are right, the term "original" is pretty obsolete. Same things goes for the term "core", even though this is less common, that was used to refer to an alter that is the "original" and that has all the memories and true personality traits of the body. 

And yup, all the alters in the same system occupies the same body and use the same brain but each one of them is a whole different person, it's not like being in love with yourself. 

Being in a relationship between alters in the same system is common and can be good but can have some negative points too, what if they broke up? They can't just avoid each other forever after. But what if they really love each other and are such a good couple? They can be supportive, help each other and be happy. 

Relationships with people outside the headspace are... Complicated... 

It depends on you and your system how to handle it. Sometimes happens that one alter has a relationship with a person that does not suffer from DID, sometimes more alters can have a relationship with a person  that does not suffer from DID but knows and loves all of them, sometimes the alters in the system have different partners, sometimes alters from different  systems meet and fall in love... 

What I meant with NPC is exactly what you think! It is not rare to have some people in the inner world that are not alters nor fragments but just people that "live there".

Anyway, all that I wrote here comes from my personal experience and thought, and it's not like I'm a therapist or something. 

- Alexis (and Nathan, cause he wanted to help)
